column1: # THE DERIVATION IS MECHANICAL
# The row counts above are not chosen: the producer emits them and
# reports the count it wrote (FIXTURE_ROW_COUNT=346).  The counts
# were then confirmed by counting the partition column of the
# produced file, partition by partition.
# THE FIXTURE WAS VERIFIED AGAINST THE REAL LEGACY ORACLE
# Before the fixture was frozen, every one of its 346 rows was
# executed against the REAL legacy astUnaryOpFromToken (compiled
# from the live src/ast.c with the delegation OFF), grouped by the
# row's initial output value:
#   GROUP A (initial 12345): 196 rows, 0 mismatches
#   GROUP B (initial 54321): 150 rows, 0 mismatches
# So the fixture does not merely CLAIM to agree with the legacy
# function: it was CHECKED against it, row by row.
# TWO DEFECTS WERE FOUND AND FIXED DURING THIS VERIFICATION
# D-FIX-01: the U04 neighbour rule originally emitted a REJECTION
# for every neighbour.  But 816 is the immediate predecessor of 817
# and is ITSELF an accepted token (TK_PRE_PLUS_PLUS).  The rule now
# asserts an accepted neighbour with its own exact enum and emits
# rejections only for genuinely unaccepted neighbours.  This was
# caught by the oracle differential, not by inspection.
# D-FIX-02: the direct literal -9223372036854775808 does NOT
# evaluate to INT64_MIN in this language: the positive magnitude is
# one past INT64_MAX, so constant folding wraps it to INT64_MIN and
# the unary minus wraps it back to -9223372036854775807.  This was
# MEASURED with a probe program.  The boundary is now reached by the
# exact arithmetic form (-9223372036854775807 - 1), and the fixture
# Both defects would have been invisible to a fixture producer that
# never ran its own output against the real legacy function.
